# Security interoperability fixtures

These PDFs exercise the Standard security handler across RC4-40 (R2), RC4-128
(R3), AES-128 (R4), AES-256-CBC (R5 and R6), and AES-256-GCM (R7). They are
generated by independent, mature PDF implementations rather than by `core-pdf`
itself: qpdf produces R2 through R6, and pyHanko produces the ISO/TS 32003:2023
AESV4/R7 fixture under `aes_gcm/`.

The committed files are the test inputs. qpdf is needed only to regenerate them
and is intentionally not a project or test dependency:

```sh
uv run python scripts/generate_security_interop_fixtures.py
```

`manifest.json` records the generating qpdf version, exact commands, test
passwords, expected content, and SHA-256 hashes. qpdf uses fresh random data
while encrypting, so regeneration may update the hashes while preserving fixture
behavior.

pyHanko is likewise an offline generator, not a project or test dependency. Its
fixture is reproducible because the generator supplies deterministic keys, salts,
and nonces for this public test data only:

```sh
uv run --with pyhanko==0.37.0 python scripts/generate_aes_gcm_interop_fixture.py
```

`aes_gcm/manifest.json` pins pyHanko 0.37.0, its release commit and MIT license,
the source and output hashes, passwords, and the exact ISO/TS 32003 security
configuration. PDF MAC is disabled to isolate ISO/TS 32003 from the unsupported
ISO/TS 32004:2024 AuthCode extension. Production code never uses deterministic
cryptographic material.

The RC4 commands include `--allow-weak-crypto` because qpdf otherwise refuses
to create those obsolete formats. R5 is also generated only to test historical
compatibility. These fixtures are read-only test inputs, not recommended PDF
creation settings.
